text: The referral is request-driven in rwb-access: the trigger of AC1 is the referral request of the fraud investigator on the referral panel of the case record, and the unattended trigger the FSD names (a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer) belongs to the case and deviation services, where X4 is raised and assigned (R-UNI-08, R-DEV-04, FEAT-DVF-04). This service starts no workflow and runs no schedule, so it claims neither, and the caller's step is a product prerequisite and not a contract of this story.
why: The FSD A2.29 step 1 says the feature receives its trigger from a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, while the ownership rows give rwb-access no event of its own, no workflow and one job only (JOB-18, the six-monthly access review), and the pattern list of this key carries neither DP-10 nor DP-14; without a default the story would either claim a schedule and an event it does not own or leave AC1 with no reachable trigger.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.29.2 and A2.29.3.3; legacy RWB-E8-018 AC1 ('When its trigger arrives'); _work/msr/context/P4.md (Events 0, Workflows 0, Jobs 1); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-08 and R-DEV-04; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-10 and DP-14
confirm: Solution architect with the tech lead of the X4 fraud routing stories (FEAT-DVF-04) at the P4 design review
impact: If the referral must run unattended, an event-started workflow on the rwb-access queue and a subscription have to be added, with the DP-10 and DP-14 dependencies raised at D1; the record, the refusals and the contract do not change.

text: Aric (INT-31, outbound, not available today) is consumed as an external operation behind a port: the contract story declares the request (referralId, caseId, caseNo, deviationCode, ruleVersion, reason) and the answer (aricReference, fraudConfirmed, reviewedAt) and the app story builds against its fake, one hop, 2 s, breaker, with the referralId as the dedupe key. The production adapter, the base URL, the media type and the authentication belong to rwb-integration (P2) under DP-16, whose contract is not in this story's dependency rows and is raised at D1 rather than added to the metadata.
why: The feature exists to send a case to an external system that the specification says is not available today, while the Work Package gives this key no X row and its C row carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON; without a default the story would either invent a Recovery service that owns Aric or stop on Day 1.
read: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (INT-31 Aric, fraud referral, out, 'not available today; by the fraud investigator'); FSD P4 v3 A2.29.2 (integration points: Aric); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-16 and section R5.4 class C and X; _work/msr/context/P4.md (P4 calls ACE Common only)
confirm: Aric owner and the tech lead of rwb-integration (P2) at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8018-CON
impact: If the interface lands in rwb-integration as a Recovery REST contract, the consumed row becomes that contract with its owner P2, the fake is replaced by that fake, and the app story and its tests are unchanged in everything but the client.

text: A referral has exactly three states - REFERRED, ANSWERED and FAILED - and an outcome is terminal; the confirmation Aric gives is one boolean (fraudConfirmed) and no outcome code vocabulary is invented, because the sources name no code set and R-DEV-13 and R-LIT-77 read only that fraud is confirmed. The referral and its outcome are two entries of the local decision-record chain, each written once and never updated, and the referralId is minted by this service and is the key Aric deduplicates on.
why: No source names a lifecycle for a referral, an outcome code set or a dedupe key, while legacy AC2 requires that nothing change when the record cannot be written and R-UNI-39 requires that no action proceed unlogged; the states, the boolean, the two-entry record and the dedupe key have to be fixed before either criterion can be built or tested.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-018 AC1 and AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.29.1 and A2.29.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DEV-13, R-LIT-77 and R-UNI-39; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03 and DP-09; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (an append-only change log)
confirm: Internal audit representative, the ledger owner of the decision-record library and the Aric owner at the contract review
impact: An outcome code set, an updatable referral or a single appended entry each change the state model, the entries and the tests; the refusals, the rights and the contract paths do not change.

text: The referral and its outcome are recorded as two entries of the DP-03 local decision-record chain in rwb_access, each with its idempotency row and its outbox row in one transaction, and each is written under the library's referral code with the referralId in the reference field of the entry; the central ledger decision_log_entry stays in rwb-decision and is neither read nor written here. The record code value itself is confirmed with the ledger owner, since no source names it.
why: Legacy AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version and AC2 requires that nothing change when it cannot be written, while the legacy key put the decision log in the monolith's own schema and the target splits it into the local chain of DP-03 and the central ledger of P7; without a default the story cannot say where the record lives or what it is written under.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-018 AC1, AC2 and its data table (decision_log_entry, DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018); FSD P4 v3 A2.29.4.1 and A2.29.4.3; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03 and DP-09 and section R3 default rulings (rule package registry with P7); TSD P4 v3 T6.3
confirm: Owner of the decision-record library and the tech lead of rwb-decision (P7) as the owner of the central ledger
impact: A different record code changes the value written on every entry and the filter the audit consumer uses; if the record had to be the central ledger instead, the story would need a P7 contract dependency at D1 and the local chain would not be written.

text: The fraud referral is authorised by a permission row of this service: Case record C for the write and Case record R for the read, resolved from role and permission in rwb_access with no hop, refused 403 with MSG-P4-002 when the letter is absent. The area and the letter are a default because TSD P4 v3 T6.1 publishes the letters of three of the 14 capability areas only and the legacy permission table of RWB-E8-018 carries the Rules and parameters rows of the rule-version template, which belong to another capability; the letter is a permission row and never a code change.
why: A referral is raised on a case and the fraud investigator is its secondary user, while the only permission table in the legacy story belongs to the rule-version feature and the technical specification's matrix does not cover the case areas; the story has to name a letter in its contract and its refusal test, or the 403 path cannot be specified.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-018 permission checks and AC-EXC-P4-029-01 (a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002); FSD P4 v3 A2.29.3.3; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T6.2; Logical Data Model v8 LOV-CAPABILITY (CASE_RECORD, first of the 14 areas); Template and Rules v1 section R3 and DP-08
confirm: Security administrator with the owner of the permission matrix at the P4 design review; a change is a permission row and not a code change
impact: If the matrix names another area or letter for a fraud referral, one permission row and the test users change and nothing else; the operation refuses on the letter it reads, so no code changes either way.
